doc.title: Eddie Miller and Pete Fountain Interview, 1970-01-09

title: Making the album: sweetening and overdubs; break
summary: After playing Traces, Pete explains the first full album with the whole band, with guitar and bass trombone added later; then a station break.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Traces, Eddie Miller with Pete Fountain's band. Is that the first time you've had a full album with the 10-piece band? Right.

It's about time. We've had two or three sides that we've done, but this is the first time with the whole of the band I'm using now, which is great. We sweetened it with the guitar player, what they call sweeten. They just put the earphones in just to add a little bit more bottom. You mean they added that later? They added that later. They added the bass trombone and the guitar.
There's a lot of that being done now. Right. It's called sweeten. With that 16-track tape now, you can do practically anything. Yeah. And you can't tell. No, you can't. There's no way to tell.
522-3791. We're going to take a short break. We have four lines open, two people waiting, and we'll be back to talk with Pete and Eddie Moore in just a moment.
